Model assumptions, equations & DQN provenance

Purpose. Compare controller response and parameter sensitivity using an empirical panel and averaged converter model. Panel ratings, charge-transfer coefficients, switch losses and capacitance are representative inputs. The included DQN is trained in this reduced environment. Validation against the full MATLAB/Simulink circuit remains separate.

Panel approximation

I(V) = Isc · [1 − (V / Voc)a], clipped to 0 ≤ V ≤ Voc. The shape factor a produces one power maximum. Vmp = Voc / (a + 1)1/a.

Isc scales with G / 1000 and an assumed +0.05%/°C coefficient. Voc uses an assumed −0.25%/°C coefficient and 0.036 ln(G/1000) irradiance term. The reference temperature is 25°C. These empirical equations are not a calibrated diode model or a specific space solar cell. G = 0 sets current and Voc to zero.

The step occurs at 45% of the run. Eclipse runs from 35% to 70%. Times are compressed demonstrations, not an orbital prediction. Temperature is constant per run. No partial shading, degradation, attitude, radiation or battery SOC model.

FSSCC approximation

Rout(f) = Rfast + k / (f · Ceff). Here f is in Hz and Ceff in F. The effective ratio m and charge-transfer coefficient k are model inputs and must be derived from the circuit topology for a calibrated model. Fibonacci ratios are explored through m; capacitor charge balance and the 10 individual switches are not simulated.

The equilibrium solves Ipv(V) = m · (mV − Vbus) / Rout, with reverse flow blocked. An ideal model-based inner loop maps each controller’s voltage reference to a bounded switching frequency. It uses the panel model at the present G and T. Both controllers receive the same ideal inner loop; this is not a measured or deployable regulator.

Voltage approaches equilibrium with an assumed first-order response time τ. Estimated bus power = Ppv · Vbus / (mV) when mV > Vbus, otherwise zero. This quasi-static loss estimate ignores transient storage, gate-drive losses, ESR ripple and switching transients. Fixed bus voltage represents an energy sink. Only pulse frequency modulation (PFM) is modeled; PWM duty and two-phase gate timing are not evaluated.

Controllers & DQN

P&O chooses the next voltage direction using measured ΔP · ΔV. DQN uses a 5 → 48 → 48 → 5 ReLU Q-network, trained in the same reduced environment. Observations are measured V / Voc, I / Isc, 5ΔP / (Voc·Isc), 5ΔV / Voc and Vref / Voc, using reference Voc and Isc. The controller does not receive the true MPP.

Training: seed 42, 208,000 transitions, replay buffer 50,000, batch 128, Adam learning rate 0.0007, discount 0.92 and target-network copy every 100 updates. Reward = Ppv / Pmpp − 0.002|action multiplier|. The true MPP is used only for training reward and evaluation. No training occurs in the browser.

Training range: G 200–1200 W/m², T 0–70°C, Voc 22–26 V, Isc 0.6–1.2 A, shape 8–16, m = 1/3, bus 4.5–5.5 V, Ceff 30–80 µF, τ 0.02–0.15 s, 0.1 s sampling, no noise and a voltage step of 1% of reference Voc. Performance outside this range is unvalidated. Exploration ε chooses a seeded random action during inference.

Metrics & reproducibility

Tracking efficiency = ∫Ppv dt / ∫Pmpp dt. Converter efficiency estimate = ∫Pbus dt / ∫Ppv dt. Integrals use the trapezoid rule. Eclipse contributes zero available energy. Fully dark runs show “N/A” for energy ratios and settling. Power ripple and settling use true simulated power, not noisy sensor samples.

Uniform independent voltage and current noise has the selected ± percentage amplitude. Both controllers use the same sensor noise sequence and initial switching frequency. The seed also fixes DQN exploration. Available MPP is an evaluation reference; reachable MPP accounts for the converter’s ratio, bus and frequency bounds.

CSV includes inputs, policy provenance, both trajectories and units. Calculations run in your browser. Changing inputs does not upload your experiment.

Background: MathWorks Solar Cell · MathWorks DQN · Seeman, switched capacitor analysis. The formulas and policy above are explicit simplifications, not implementations supplied by these sources.
